clue.text: Some impressive picture

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, signalling a run concealed inside them

explanation.surface: A remark praising part of a striking painting or photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters spanning the end of 'impressive' and the start of 'picture'; read whole, the clue also defines the answer as a grand film.
explanation.definitionFit: A film on a grand, spectacular scale is called an epic, so it is an impressive picture.

clue.text: Apply without pressure, as one with particular proficiency

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the word for apply wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to apply force or effort is to exert it
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Advice to use something gently, as a skilled specialist would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: EXERT goes around P.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist with great skill in a particular field is an expert.

clue.text: Confused blog stated it's a kind of fuel

indicators.note: something confused is jumbled up, so the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says a muddled weblog claimed something was a type of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges the ten letters of BLOG STATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane or butane sold in cylinders is a common fuel for camping stoves and heaters.

clue.text: Sign agreement to strike, overturning excuse

indicators.note: turning something over puts it the other way round, so the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a nod of the head signals agreement
to rap is to hit sharply

explanation.surface: A call to sign a deal to stop a walkout, reversing an earlier excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign agreement to strike' reads like industrial relations; 'overturning' reverses NOD + RAP as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to forgive or let off, the same as to pardon.

clue.text: Awfully bad girl pinching ring one imprisoned repeatedly

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip or nip, so the jumbled letters hold the next piece inside them
something done awfully is done badly, so the letters of the following two words are jumbled

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A wicked young woman steals a ring and keeps being locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges BAD GIRL into GALBIRD, and 'pinching' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual criminal who has spent many terms behind bars is called a gaolbird (jailbird), British spelling.

clue.text: 2, 24 across and 4, oddly, as opposed to 8

definitions.meaning: each of these clue answers is one of the plural sense: an expert, an advantage, and the odd letters of the answer to 4 down (first, third, fifth) spell the short word for a professional
the answer to 8 down is the disadvantages, and the two words form the stock pair for arguments for and against

explanation.walkthrough: Cross-references: 2 is EXPERT, 24 across ADVANTAGE, 4 down PARDON, whose odd letters give PRO; 8 is CONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Professionals and advantages are both called pros, and pros are the case for, as opposed to cons, the case against.

clue.text: Work quietly on early bid as rival

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
in the card game bridge, one no-trump (1NT) is an opening bid made early in the auction

explanation.surface: Advice to labour silently on a first offer, as a competitor would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early bid' is the bridge bid one no-trump, written ONE NT; 'on' just joins the pieces. Bridge is a card game in which players bid before play.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone you compete against, so a rival.

clue.text: Business partners, such as 5, 11 and 17

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Fellow members of a firm, offered as examples of something.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are the two partners facing each other in bridge. The three examples are GAOLBIRD (a convict), CHEAT and STING, all cons in some sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaolbird is a convict, a cheat is a con man, and a sting is a con or swindle.

clue.text: Panorama broadcast about vote for a period of stability

indicators.note: means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the mark for a vote
something broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters of the programme name are spread into a new order

parts.note: Panorama is a long-running BBC current affairs programme, taken here as written
a cross, X, is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A TV documentary programme is aired about an election, spanning a calm era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' sits naturally next to Panorama, the BBC current affairs show, but it signals the anagram; 'about' puts X inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names the long era of relative peace across the Roman Empire, so a time of stability.

clue.text: Contemporary copies held by literature professor

indicators.note: the letters are contained inside the following words, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Modern reprints are kept by a literature lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'literature' and the start of 'professor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for reproduction, it means a modern copy of an older piece of furniture or art.

clue.text: Constant intense pressure for dishonest person

parts.note: C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to be under heat, or have the heat on, is to face intense pressure

explanation.surface: Being under constant strain drives someone to be dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who swindles or plays unfairly is a cheat, a dishonest person.

clue.text: They will profoundly mislead you, unless I do otherwise

indicators.note: means in a different way, so the letters of the preceding words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A warning that things will badly deceive you unless you act differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do otherwise' reads as a phrase, but 'do' is part of the fodder UNLESSIDO and 'otherwise' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: False beliefs held firmly against evidence deceive the mind deeply, so they profoundly mislead.

clue.text: A little seabird or marsh bird

parts.note: a bit means a small amount
a tern is a gull-like seabird

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is a small seabird or a wetland bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like bird of reedbeds and marshes known for its booming call.

clue.text: In period of prosperity, bury small chest

indicators.note: burying something puts it inside, so the time of prosperity holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a boom is a time of rapid economic growth
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Advice to hide a little treasure chest while times are good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests a box to bury, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom is the human chest or breast.

clue.text: Make some changes in speech to spread ill-feeling about left

indicators.note: means surrounding, so the word for spreading ill-feeling wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to infect is to pass on disease, or a bad mood, to others

explanation.surface: Someone alters their tone of voice to stir up resentment against the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflect is to vary the pitch or tone of the voice, or change a word's form for grammar.

clue.text: Value of bar seen in drunken state as propitious

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone judges a pub's worth while drunk and finds it promising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drunken state' rearranges VALUEOFBAR; 'seen' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Propitious conditions are favourable ones, likely to bring success.

clue.text: Old American model poses for work assignments

parts.note: the Model T was an early Ford car made in America
to pose a question is to ask it

explanation.surface: A vintage Yankee mannequin strikes poses for jobs to be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' and 'poses' suggest fashion, but the model is Ford's Model T car and 'poses' means puts questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work set for someone, so work assignments.

clue.text: Time in prison reduced by exactly 50% for venomous attack

indicators.note: the time abbreviation goes inside the shortened prison name
cutting the prison name exactly in half keeps only its first half, one of the two repeated words

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous maximum-security prison in New York State

explanation.surface: A prison term is cut in half, and the convict strikes back viciously.
explanation.walkthrough: Halving SING SING leaves SING, and 'in' puts T inside it. 'Time in prison' sounds like a sentence served, but it gives T and the prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is the venom-injecting wound from a bee, wasp or scorpion.

clue.text: Do something creative, based on instinct, about old volume

indicators.note: means around, so the word for instinctive goes around the other pieces

parts.note: innate qualities are inborn, coming from instinct rather than learning

explanation.surface: Advice to make something original by following your gut and an old book.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce new ideas or methods, a creative act.

clue.text: Finally at short notice producing a small amount

indicators.note: means at the end, taking just the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: ad, short for advertisement, is a brief notice

explanation.surface: Something achieved at the last minute yields only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at short notice' reads as one phrase, but 'Finally' takes the last letter of 'at' and 'short notice' is an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a little bit, a very small quantity.

clue.text: As one who's left, critically examine a Conservative cut

parts.note: to test something is to examine it critically

indicators.note: means shortened, so the last letter of the word for a Conservative is removed

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A party member who has defected looks over a Conservative cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' suggests departed or left-wing, but it means left things in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will and leaves property to heirs.

clue.text: Some upset over reversing 25 and 27

indicators.note: means read backwards, so the run taken from the words is turned round
only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Some people are upset at the overturning of a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the reversal signal, but it is part of the text; 'Some' takes SETOV from 'upset over' and 'reversing' turns it round. 25 and 27 are NAYS and AYES.
explanation.definitionFit: Noes and yeses cast in a ballot are both kinds of ballot cast in a division.

clue.text: Drawbacks in writing about having current employment

indicators.note: means surrounding, so the abbreviation for writing goes around the other piece

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
something in use is currently employed, being used now

explanation.surface: Written drawbacks of a job someone is doing at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' before 'writing' only joins; IN USE is the phrase meaning currently employed.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuses are disadvantages, negative points weighed against positives.

clue.text: They indicate additions, including extra line in Cats

indicators.note: means containing, so the word for cats holds the next piece inside

parts.note: pusses are cats, from puss
L is the abbreviation for line, here an extra one

explanation.surface: A theatre note about an added line in the musical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' suggests the stage musical, but it is the animals, PUSSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus signs are the symbols showing that numbers are to be added.

clue.text: Have greater regard for judge interrupting jury member half-heartedly?

indicators.note: breaking into the middle of something, so the judge goes inside the shortened word
half the heart is removed, so one of the two middle letters of the word is dropped

parts.note: a jury is traditionally made up of one's peers, so a juror is a peer
a ref, short for referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a juror who is not fully committed respects the judge more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jury member' rests on the idea of being tried by a jury of one's peers; 'half-heartedly' cuts one of the two middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer one thing is to like it more than another, to regard it more highly.

clue.text: 8 animals in herd

definitions.meaning: the answer to 8 down is used as a verb: to con (or conn) a ship is to direct its course
bullocks raised for beef, kept in herds

explanation.walkthrough: 8 is CONS, read as the nautical verb meaning directs a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Directing a ship's course is to steer it, and young castrated bulls kept for beef are steers.

clue.text: Bit of proverbial wisdom about very diligent worker creating profit

indicators.note: means surrounding, so the saying goes around the other pieces

parts.note: an adage is a traditional saying, a nugget of proverbial wisdom
the ant is proverbially hard-working

explanation.surface: A wise saying about the industrious worker leading to gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diligent worker' is the ant, the proverbial model of hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage is a benefit or gain, so profit in the broad sense.

clue.text: 7 cannot win, being oddly deficient

indicators.note: lacking the odd-numbered letters, so only the even-placed letters are kept

explanation.surface: Someone who is lacking in an odd way cannot succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of 'cannot win' leaves the even ones. 7 is OPPONENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against something is anti, an opponent of it.

clue.text: Denials beginning now, as you speak

indicators.note: the beginnings of the words are taken, the first letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: Refusals start right now, while you are talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' applies to all four words: now, as, you, speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Nays are no votes, refusals or denials.

clue.text: Retrospectively, a time and a place for sporting contest

indicators.note: looking back means reading backwards, so the following pieces are reversed

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Looking back, a particular moment and location for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a time' gives AN ERA, which 'Retrospectively' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed area where sports events and contests are held.

clue.text: One or more positive responses

parts.note: a single yes vote, or several, the word works as one person's yes or a count of yes votes in Parliament

explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament votes in favour are counted as the yes side, a word for positive replies.

clue.text: Start of trial with legal representative in poor condition

indicators.note: takes the beginning, the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: atty is the abbreviation for attorney, a lawyer

explanation.surface: At the opening of a court case, the defendant and lawyer look shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tatty is worn and shabby, in poor condition.

clue.text: Concerning learner — changed gear too much

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
L is the learner-driver plate

indicators.note: the letters of the following word are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Worries about a learner driver who shifted gear too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed gear' suggests driving, but 'changed' rearranges GEAR into ARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlarge means too big, excessive in size, so too much.
